t: 3797. Count Routes to Climb a Rectangular Grid
o: Count routes from any open cell in the bottom row to the top row. Moves go up one row (column shift with 1 + dc^2 <= d^2) or slide horizontally within a row (|dc| <= d), but never two horizontal slides in a row. For ["..","#."], d=1 there are 2 routes; with d=2 there are 4 since diagonal (sqrt 2) hops unlock; a fully blocked start row gives 0; a single open row gives 4 (two starts, plus horizontal slides each way). Row-by-row DP with two states - arrived-by-vertical (or start) vs arrived-by-horizontal - plus sliding-window prefix sums handles n, m, d up to 750 in O(n*m).
k: Two DP states per cell: A = ways whose last move was vertical/start, B = ways whose last move was horizontal; horizontal moves may only depart from A.
Upward moves from row r+1 to r may shift columns by at most rv = floor(sqrt(d^2 - 1)); horizontal slides by at most d.
Both windows are computed with per-row prefix sums, giving O(1) transitions per cell.
Blocked cells contribute 0 and are simply skipped.

a.n: Approach 1: Layered DP with sliding-window prefix sums
a.i: Process rows bottom-up. A[r][c] = sum of A+B over the vertical window in row r+1; B[r][c] = sum of A over the horizontal window in row r minus A[r][c] (staying put is not a move). Start row initializes A = 1 on open cells; the answer is the total of A+B on the top row.
s: Compute rv = floor(sqrt(d^2 - 1)) for the vertical column radius.
Initialize A = 1, B = 0 on open cells of the bottom row.
For each row upward: A[c] = window sum of (A+B) from the row below within rv; then B[c] = window sum of the new A within d, minus A[c].
Return (sum of A + sum of B) on row 0 modulo 1e9+7.
a.t: O(n * m) - each cell does O(1) window work via prefix sums, across n row layers
a.sp: O(m) for the rolling row arrays and prefix sums

w: Emphasize the two-state trick enforcing 'no two consecutive horizontal moves' - collapsing to one state would overcount. Pitfalls: computing the vertical radius (floor(sqrt(d^2-1)), which is 0 when d = 1), remembering a horizontal 'move' cannot have dc = 0 (subtract self), negative modulo results in C++/Java, and routes that start and end on the same single-row grid (example 4). Follow-up: moves also downward, or count routes visiting a special cell.
